selection_rationale: P4 is the only candidate that kept 100% of readme:v4's genuine README use items and true SUPPORTED probes on every seen set (R4 DEV 31/31, G22-R2 DEV 20/20 and EVAL 19/19, VAL-1 36/36, VAL-2 23/23; G22-R README recall 14/14 and 12/12) while cutting false SUPPORTED to 3 / 0 / 0 / 4 / 3 on those sets.

exact_rejection_rules.scope: only occurrences whose surface lowercases to one of the 11 README-ambiguous aliases (react express swift rust ruby shell torch python java flask pandas); every other alias = readme:v4 exactly; the production 8D.3 filter still applies first; a rejected occurrence falls through to the next occurrence / alias (production code)
exact_rejection_rules.implementation: scripts/evaluation_lib/m11g22r4_policies.py explain(text, start, end, level); P4 = level 4
exact_rejection_rules.P1_homonym: per-alias lexicon HOMONYM, consulted only in a fixed position: adjacent modifier before; adjacent head noun after; 3-word after-window (pandas animal nouns only); bounded before/after frames (verb, adjective, transit, corrosion, carry senses; some also require the alias to be lowercase as an ADDITIONAL necessary condition); coordinated homonym sibling; personal / pet name frame; determiner-headed count noun (a/an/another, or lowercase the/each/every/possessive, at most one gap word outside a stop list, alias followed by punctuation / conjunction / preposition / pronoun / auxiliary; python swift shell torch flask ruby java only; never 'Ruby on Rails')
exact_rejection_rules.P2_negation: negator (no/not/without/never/nor/neither/n't forms) within 3 words before the alias in the same clause (clause cut at , ; : ( ) dashes but however although though whereas while) unless the gap holds an exception / causal word; or '<alias>-free'; or '<alias> [<=2 words] is/are/was not|isn't used/required/needed/necessary/involved/included/installed/supported/bundled/a dependency'
exact_rejection_rules.P3_attribution: reference / comparison frame immediately before (inspired by, modelled on, borrowed from, ported from, port/clone/fork/rewrite of, alternative to, replacement for, similar to, think of it as, comparing, than, as X as, compared to, versus/vs, instead of, rather than, in place of, + <=2 determiners/qualifiers); 'like' + determiners or a short list; historical frames (originally/initially/formerly/previously, began life as, moved/migrated/switched/ported off|from, old/former/previous, until vN, first prototype used, no longer, used to); future frames (plan/hope/intend to, would like to, aim to, going to, eventually, someday, in the future, todo, wishlist, will be ported to with <=3-word gap in clause; considering / evaluating / investigating / migrating..to / can be generated for: immediately before); after-frames ('<alias> [bindings|port|support|...] would/could/will be' except installed/used/required/needed/downloaded/built/compiled/fetched, 'can be generated', 'is/are planned|coming|on the roadmap|not yet available...'); unchecked task-list line '- [ ]'; other-project docs ('notes|cheat sheet|translation|summary|documentation|docs|reading notes|reading group on|about|of|for [how|the]'; 'the [official] <alias> documentation|docs|handbook|book|internals|foundation|community|conference|core team'; '<alias> ... maintained|written|developed|owned|published by another|other|a different|a separate|a third|someone'); blockquote line introduced by a line ending ':' or under a said/testimonial/quote/feedback/review/excerpt/notice heading; '[project](https://...) (<alias>)'; list item with an external URL (itself or nested sub-items) under a bindings/ports/wrappers/implementations/community/third-party/ecosystem/used by/who uses/showcase/in the wild/projects using/other languages heading (ATX or setext)
exact_rejection_rules.P4_overrides: a P1 rejection is withdrawn if: code span/fence; version string immediately after; claim-of-use frame immediately before (G22-R2 _USE_FRAME); coordinated with a registry technology (G22-R2 _registry_list_sibling); software head noun immediately after. A P3 'like' rejection is withdrawn if a claim-of-use verb opens the clause before 'like'. P2 and all other P3 rules are never overridden.
exact_rejection_rules.sentence_model: research-only paragraph-aware sentence span: soft-wrapped newlines join; blank lines, list items, headings, blockquotes, tables, fences and setext underlines break; e.g./i.e./vs./etc./cf. do not end a sentence

acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.G1_genuine_readme_use_retention: P4 keeps >= 95% of the genuine README use items (concept-level README items labelled 'use') that readme:v4 extracts
acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.G2_true_supported_retention: P4 keeps >= 95% of readme:v4's true SUPPORTED probes
acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.G3_false_supported_reduction: P4 false SUPPORTED <= 50% of readme:v4's (at least 50% fewer)
acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.G4_no_new_false_supported: every P4 false SUPPORTED control is also false SUPPORTED under readme:v4
acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.G5_corroborated: every artifact-corroborated used probe stays SUPPORTED
acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.G6_non_ambiguous: no README item of a non-ambiguous alias differs from readme:v4
acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.G7_g19_capability: G19 capability identical for all 39 concepts and all 64 README-safe aliases still extracted from 'This project is built with <alias>.'
acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.G8_no_job_side_regression: job parsing identical on every G22 corpus (G22-Q, G22, G21, G20, G17, G16, G15, M10/M10E) under P4
acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.uncertain_handling: controls whose probe is labelled uncertain are excluded from G2-G5 (G22-R2/R3 harness convention) and reported separately
acceptance_gates_on_fresh_set_declared_b.decision_rule: ALL gates must pass for a positive research recommendation; if any fails, P4 as frozen is not recommended for readme:v5; thresholds are not changed after the run; any revision needs a NEW fresh set

threshold_justification: The milestone brief's suggested high-recall gates are adopted unchanged; no different threshold was found to be scientifically justified.
secondary_metrics: occurrence level: author-labelled valid use occurrences rejected and invalid occurrences rejected, each with its rule reason
D and R3 on the same fresh set (comparison only)
known_limitations: Long-tail homonym senses outside the lexicon stay false ('Swift onboarding is the goal', 'React, record, repeat', 'ruby for the fortieth', 'a start port on Java', 'the python every ten days').
Other-project documentation without a bounded frame stays false ('documentation site of Quarry, a Java persistence library').
Non-ambiguous aliases are out of scope by gate G6, so 'plan to add a PyTorch backend', 'Inspired by FastAPI' and 'No Docker needed' stay false.
'Java coffee ... app' is rejected by the 'Java coffee' head-noun rule even when a reader would call it ambiguous.
'Photos taken in Java last summer' and 'Ruby, our app's mascot' are kept (no bounded rule).
The homonym lexicon is alias-specific metadata that would need a production home; the sentence model and setext-heading index differ from production readme_context.
The fresh set's author is the same model family as the policy author; it is not human-independent.
